news.title: Leandro Paredes handed massive punishment for World Cup Final brawl
news.lede: Leandro Paredes has received a lengthy ban for his role in the post-FIFA World Cup Final 2026 brawl. After Argentina fell short against Spain at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, USA, the defender engaged in a heated scuffle with members of the opposing team. While the World Cup final is designed to create action on the field, it was the drama that unfolded after the match that provided the biggest fireworks display of the evening. In a moment of madness, a furious Leandro Paredes grabbed Eric Garcia by the throat before launching Gavi towards the ground.

news.title: World Cup coming home? England prepares potential bid to host 2038 or 2042
news.lede: The long wait for a home tournamentAccording to The Sun , Great Britain is considering a bid to host either the 2038 or 2042 World Cup. Supported by Prime Minister Andy Burnham, the proposal aims to bring football's flagship tournament back to British soil for the first time since 1966. With Burnham reportedly viewing a World Cup bid as a key driver for national investment, tourism, and urban regeneration, the tournament could finally return to British shores. Beyond its global tourist appeal and well-established transport network, Britain already possesses the world-class stadium infrastructure needed to host a tournament of this scale.The UK has not hosted the men's World Cup since 1966, although England hosted Euro 1996 and Wembley Stadium staged the Euro 2020 final.

news.title: FIFA World Cup final brawl: Leandro Paredes suspended for 10 matches, Argentina fined $321,000
news.lede: Argentine football player Leandro Paredes has been slapped with a 10-match suspension for being involved in a brawl after his team lost to Spain in the World Cup final received a 10-match suspension for his part in a brawl after his team lost to Spain in the World Cup final last month. His teammate Nahuel Molina has also been suspended for seven games, FIFA announced on Friday. A scuffle erupted following the final whistle when Argentina midfielder Paredes pushed Spain's Gavi to the ground as the European champions' substitutes rushed onto the field to celebrate. Paredes was charged on three assault counts, while Molina faced two.

news.title: European FAs reveal U20 Women's World Cup squads despite UEFA boycott
news.lede: UEFA announced it would boycott all FIFA tournaments after FIFA president Gianni Infantino announced plans to sell part of the FIFA World Cup through FIFA Forward Enterprise, a $20 billion subsidiary that would sell 20 per cent of the tournament to private investors. The 55 UEFA members unanimously voted to boycott FIFA tournaments as long as the sell-off plans were on the table, and UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin said they would keep up the boycott after FIFA and Infantino withdrew the plans, saying conditions had not been met. "First, the proposals to sell off the major competitions had to be withdrawn, and secondly, assurances have to be made that such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again. These conditions have not been met," Ceferin said in a statement.

news.title: Epilogue of the conflict at the end of the World Cup final: Paredes will not play 10 matches, the Argentine Football Association must pay $321.000
news.lede: The International Football Federation (FIFA) has imposed sanctions a month after the World Cup final between Argentina and Spain due to a major on-field clash after the match. The most severely punished was Argentina international Leandro Paredes, who received a 10-match suspension. His teammate Nahuel Molina will not be able to play in the next seven matches, while Thiago Almada was suspended for one match, reported Spanish outlet Marca. Argentina was defeated by Spain 1-0 in the World Cup final.

news.title: Argentina hit with heavy sanctions by FIFA for World Cup controversies
news.lede: Leando Paredes banned for 10 international matches and fined, along with teammate Nahuel Molina, who gets seven games; AFA ordered to play one national team match without fans for Malvinas flag incident, Thiago Almada and Spain’s Gavi given one-match bans. FIFA's Disciplinary Committee has imposed sanctions on the Argentine Football Association (AFA), three members of the national team squad and one of its coaches following incidents that occurred after Argentina's defeat by Spain in the 2026 World Cup final. Midfielder Leandro Paredes and two other Argentina players have received bans and fines for their involvement in clashes with Spain players after the final whistle, FIFA confirmed on Friday. Argentina have also been ordered to play their next two home matches with a 50 percent cap on spectator attendance, although one match of the sanction has been suspended.
